issues.body:
This issue tracks extending the hero run ([#8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435)) from 65K to 262,144-token context. Run status lives in [#8506](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8506). The recipe research lives in [logbooks #37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37). The 65K switch was [#10821](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10821) and [#10820](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10820).

## Plan

Train two recipes one after the other from step 390251 to step 393491, 3,240 steps or 149.5B tokens each, then compare them. Each finalist runs on 11 racks with context parallelism 4 and expert parallelism 16 (CP4 × EP16) and 16 sequences per rack, so 176 in all, and takes about 27 h at 29.9 s/step with saves (estimate).

Parent: `hero-ctx65k-step372k`, final checkpoint `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-step372k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-390251`. The merged start is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/checkpoints/step-390251`, an equal-weight hyperball average of the last 11 permanent checkpoints (details on [#8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6676769570)).

## Status

First finalist `hero-lce-global184-step390k` is launching from main at `e0bc917ee5`, about 21:40 UTC on 2026-11-06. Go or no-go follows on #8506.

Second finalist `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k` launches after it, at `0454bdd609` on the branch of draft [#11044](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11044), when the first ends.

Both appear in the W&B report, [Hero 262K finalists](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Hero-262K-finalists--VmlldzoxODI2NjQ1Nw==).

## Configuration

| Field | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| First finalist | Global 1.84: `qk_mult` 1.66, long scale 1.108 | Merged, [#11041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11041) |
| Second finalist | Log floor 65536, slope 0.1, power 2, global layers | Branch; merges only if it wins, at the comparison on Monday 2026-11-09 |
| Start | Merged checkpoint at step 390251 | Merged, #11041 |
| Loader queue | 64 batches, down from 512 | Merged, #11041 |
| Run length | 3,240 steps, stop step 393491, 149.5B tokens | Merged, #11041 |
| Learning rate | Linear from 5% to 1% of peak over the 3,240 steps | Merged; the #11041 review approved the PR that states it |
| Router bias | Updates each step, as before | A frozen-bias arm was not adopted |
| Evals | In-loop at 262K every 500 steps, with a final eval at the stop | Padded windows and multi-length evals are not in this launch |
| Checkpoints | Seven permanent, about 30 TB per finalist (inferred) | Merged, #11041 |
| Data | Documents above 65,536 tokens at 4× sampling weight, 43.9% of tokens | [#10980](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10980), merged |
| Capacity factor | 1.5 | Unchanged |

The earlier switches set `qk_mult` from 1.3 × (1 + 0.1 ln(N/4096)) on all layers: 1.48 at 16K and 1.66 at 65K. Global 1.84 takes the value that rule gives at 262K and applies it to global layers only. No training arm ran it. It lies between Keep 1.66 and Global 1.88, which were trained.

## Evidence

Seven 100-step arms at 11 racks, on the launch data mix, from step 390251: six recipes from the merged checkpoint and Keep 1.66 (`qk_mult` unchanged) from the raw one. Each arm is one seed. "Global X" means global layers at X and other layers at 1.66. Clean macro is the mean loss over 19 held-out subsets. MRCR is the paired retrieval eval from [#8701](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8701); full NLL is its loss with the whole document in context, and recovery is the share of the evidence's benefit that survives in a long document. The logbook defines these fully. The [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2307cd320fb832c022284d6df07858db3b89d5f/logbooks/37-hero-262k/notebook.md) has full tables, commands, commits and negative results. W&B: `hero-lce11*` and `hero-mrcr-lce11*` in [`marin_moe`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe).

- Held-out text does not separate the merged recipes. Clean macro at 262K spans 0.0004 (1.6451 to 1.6455), against checkpoint jitter of 0.0002 to 0.0007.
- Retrieval (MRCR full NLL) differences survive correction across documents only, since no arm was repeated. The second finalist is 0.0017 below Keep 1.66 (corrected p 0.002) and 0.0014 below Global 1.88 (corrected p 0.001). Global 1.88 is not separated from Keep 1.66 (corrected p 1.00).
- Recovery does not separate the arms from Keep 1.66 after correction. It is 0.982 to 0.984 everywhere.
- The merged start was 0.0017 lower on clean macro than raw after 100 steps, down from about 0.003, on one seed. It may not last the run. Retrieval did not change.
- Raising the scale produces gradient spikes in the first two steps: 6.31 for Global 1.88 and 19.65 for the second finalist, against 0.62 for Keep 1.66. Gradients are clipped at 1.0. Whether this matters past 100 steps is not known.
- Holding the router bias at the merged checkpoint's value, in one more 100-step arm against the merged Global 1.88 arm, was not adopted. The rule, fixed before submission, needed clean macro better by more than 0.0007, and the change was 0.00015. Drops were 1.05x, under the 2x reject line. Full NLL was 0.0010 lower [-0.0015, -0.0006]. That arm's grad norm reached 83.56 on one step, against 0.19 in the control. The cause is unexplained, and one run cannot show whether freezing caused it.
- Memory: the train loader's 512-batch queue lives in device memory, and growth largely ends when it first wraps. One batch leaves per step, so queue 64 wraps every 64 steps. At queue 64 the tightest of 704 devices had 3.86 GiB free, against 2.08 GiB at 512, in runs that differ in recipe and start. On one rack at queue 64, a slow remainder of growth reached zero by the fourth wrap. Trimming the memory pool did not stop growth.

## Not tested

1. Global 1.84 in training. No rehearsal ran, so this launch is the first GPU training run of its recipe and of the code at `e0bc917ee5`.
2. Any 11-rack run past 100 steps, so also the queue-64 memory trend at 11 racks past its first wrap.
3. The learning-rate schedule at this length. The arms ran the same 5% start on a 4,335-step schedule, so this run's rate falls about 34% faster per step.
4. The 11-rack stop path. `HERO_SCHEDULE_EXTENSION` ([#10917](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10917), merged) was tested on one rack, on an earlier deploy head.
5. SFT and RL loading of the merged checkpoint, for any recipe.
6. Export of the second finalist. Hero exports refuse log scaling until serving support lands, so that checkpoint cannot be served yet. [#10986](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10986) (open) adds the slope and power fields.
7. Repeats. No arm has a second seed, so training noise at 11 racks is unmeasured.
8. Code on the launch commit that no arm ran. This includes #10556, which skips short-convolution weight gradients for frozen weights. Hero weights are not frozen, and reading the source and a CPU check with stand-in kernels show no effect. We did not check compiled GB200 code. It also includes [#11054](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11054), which changes only how eval macros are computed on the host after the eval loop.

## Reading the first evals

Training evals drop each corpus's final partial window, so `ptb` and `wikitext_103` have no window at 262K and write no online value. [#10711](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10711), which adds padded windows and multi-length evals, is not in this launch. Offline evals pad instead, so they still score both subsets.

- `eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` excludes both subsets, which moves the parent's 1.960 to 2.043 at step 390251 with no change in the model.
- The `eval_regressed` alert compares each eval with the previous two, so it should fire on the child's first two evals for that reason, the first near step 390500 and about 2 h in. It is expected, and it does not show a regression. No run has shown it yet.
- `eval_dropless/macro_loss` now excludes both subsets too (#11054), and read 1.85 on the first eval, at W&B step 390499. The 100-step arms averaged them in as zeros and read about 1.78, so that series is not comparable with theirs.
- In-loop and offline levels differ. In the arms, the in-loop eval read 0.0040 above the offline eval on the 12 clean Paloma subsets. The finalist comparison uses offline evals.

The `throughput_low` alert has a floor of 2.0M tokens per second, and this run trains at about 1.58M, so it should also fire for as long as the floor stands. It does not affect training.

## Gates

These values are confirmed.

| When | Check | Expected | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Restore | One coordinator; restored step 390251 from the merged path; optimizer counts match | | Any mismatch |
| First steps | Train cross-entropy; step time; drop fraction; learning rate | Cross-entropy below 1.25; about 29 s/step; near the arms' 2.9e-4; 5% of peak | Cross-entropy at or above 1.25 |
| First hour | Optimizer, learning-rate and parameter-norm graphs, read by eye | No step or jump | Reviewer judgment |
| About 33 min into training | Largest device memory in use after the first queue wrap | Near 179.4 GiB | Above 180 GiB means queue 64 did not land |
| After the first eval and each restart | Largest device memory in use, of 184.30 GiB | 180.44 GiB; pass up to 180.75 | Above 182.25 GiB |

There is no matched control: the parent ended at step 390251. Compare with the parent's last steps and the 11-rack arms at matching steps.

## Checklist

### A. Decisions

- [x] **A1** Start from the merged checkpoint.
- [x] **A2** Finalists and their order.
- [x] **A3** Loader queue 64.
- [x] **A4** Learning-rate schedule.
- [x] **A5** Frozen router bias: not adopted.
- [ ] **A6** Gates, and go or no-go for the second finalist.

### B. Code

- [x] **B1** [#10917](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10917) stop step, merged as `7903eda6d1`.
- [x] **B2** Deploy PR for the first finalist, [#11041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11041), merged as `cac11d381a`: `HERO_MODEL`, schedule extension, `HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES`, `HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL`, `current_run.py`, `trigger_hero.sh`.
- [x] **B3** [#11054](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11054) eval macros, merged as `e0bc917ee5`, the launch commit.
- [ ] **B4** Second finalist: [#11044](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11044), a branch carrying [#10986](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10986), merged only if it wins.
- [ ] **B5** Serving support for log scaling, before SFT or RL uses the second finalist.

### C. Tests

- [x] **C1** Seven 100-step arms at 11 racks, and one frozen-bias arm.
- [x] **C2** Stop path on one rack, on an earlier deploy head (`d0d4e15f45`).
- [ ] **C3** SFT and RL load test of the merged checkpoint. Not required for this launch; still to do.

### D. Launch, for each finalist

- [ ] **D1** Fork W&B once from the parent at `_step` 390250, the row for the last update before restored step 390251.
- [x] **D2** Publish the W&B comparison report before the first step: [Hero 262K finalists](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Hero-262K-finalists--VmlldzoxODI2NjQ1Nw==), one report for both finalists.
- [ ] **D3** Launch; confirm one coordinator, the restore at step 390251 and the first steps.
- [ ] **D4** Read the gates and post go or no-go to #8506.

### E. Afterwards

- [ ] **E1** Compare the finalists on Paloma, Uncheatable and MRCR at matching steps, using offline evals. Record the winner here, on logbooks #37 and on #8435.
- [ ] **E2** Seal each run. Update the logbook conclusion and the `marin-logbooks` index.

## Stop and recovery

A failed gate stops the finalist. After a fix, relaunch from step-390251 with a new run ID, or from the child's newest complete checkpoint if the fault is an ordinary interruption. Do not fork W&B again for a retry of the same run. There is no parent run to return to, since the 65K run has ended.

The November 6 Tier 2 ferry failed in `datakit/quality/tier2-skewed`. After Iris lost a worker, Zephyr released its replacement workers while four map shards still belonged to the lost worker. The quality stage stopped at 115/119 shards and the ferry exited 1. This is the Tier 2 recurrence of #10974. Classification: controller bug, triggered by an Iris worker failure.

Reproduce:
1. Start a final-stage Zephyr map with `drain_idle_workers=True`; let worker A hold the last shard.
2. Lose A's Iris worker and start replacement B before A's 120-second heartbeat expires.
3. B gets `SHUTDOWN` while A still owns the shard. After the timeout, the shard requeues with no worker left. A local probe on `6f62a629` produced `first=RUN_TASK; replacement=SHUTDOWN; requeued=1; completed=0/1`, followed by `Worker job terminated permanently`.

Expected: A replacement worker stays available to process shards requeued after the failed worker's heartbeat expires.

<details><summary>Run evidence</summary>

- Iris marked four quality worker tasks (3, 4, 20, 42) for retry at 18:10:57 UTC after their TPU worker exceeded the reconcile failure threshold. All four replacement tasks succeeded; the worker job reported 119/119 tasks succeeded.
- Finelog `marin` / `log`, 18:10:40–18:12:30 UTC: replacement task `20:1` received `SHUTDOWN` at 18:11:27 (seq `30841684615`); the coordinator aborted at 18:11:39 with 115/119 shards complete (seq `30841686524`); the original workers missed heartbeats at 18:11:54–57 (seq `30841692099`–`30841692110`). These are event rows, not counters. The hub rows have an empty `cluster` field.
- [Actions diagnostics artifact](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42237530145/artifacts/13531227614) and [Zephyr drain predicate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f62a629e157b91cb170d6733e959f48b5d88906/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/coordinator.py#L908-L927).
- [Echo incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/944).

</details>

## Canary run context

- Lane: `datakit-tier2` (GCP, us-west4); date: 2026-11-06 UTC
- Iris job: `/runner/iris-run-job-20261106-145119`
- [GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42237530145)
- [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/datakit-tier2-ferry-42237530145-1) (configured ID; creation not verified)

issues.author: yonromai
issues.body:
## Summary This issue is the execution tracker for measuring GrugMoE architecture choices that must be fixed before pretraining. It does not choose the training model; it asks the inference team to benchmark a frozen validation anchor from PR #7820 on GB200, establish benchmark health with rolling R3-off repeatability plus separate production-like chat-R3 controls, then run a bounded sequence of architecture comparisons: serving topology, KV heads, global-attention frequency, sliding window, SConv4, lightweight blocks, and modeling-gated P1 candidates. The controlling protocol is #7912, which defines plateau throughput, routing controls, required artifacts, and acceptance gates. Work is incomplete until valid result packets support an inference recommendation to modeling before architecture freeze. ### Helpful links - [Benchmark protocol #7912](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7912) - [Merged validation-anchor PR #7820](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7820) - [Provisional pretraining and RL timelines #7673](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7673) > [!IMPORTANT] > The inference team measures cost and makes recommendations. Modeling owns > quality constraints and the final pretraining architecture. The anchor below > is a stable A/B reference, not a selected training model. ## Validation anchor | Property | Frozen value | | --- | --- | | Shape | Hidden size 6,144; 48 layers | | Attention | 48 query heads; 12 local / 6 global KV heads; five local layers per global layer; window 512 | | Routed experts | Top-4 of 128; intermediate size 3,072 | | Shared experts | Two separate half-width experts; intermediate size 3,072 each | | Other blocks | Global NoPE, local half-RoPE, `sconv4`, attention gate, exclusive self-attention, frozen QB routing bias, gated norms | | Serving | Trunk logits only; `PP1 TP1 DP16 EP16`; BF16 weights and KV cache on four `gb200-4x` nodes | Merged [PR #7820](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7820) defines this exact shape. The protocol's preflight evidence shows that it can start and generate. It does not show that modeling selected it or that dummy weights predict trained-model performance. ## Required experiments Run in this order when capacity is scarce. Check a box only after linking a valid result packet and recording the inference recommendation. - [ ] **0 · Benchmark health.** Pass two identical rolling R3-off reference arms within 2%, then measure the reference with the production-like chat-R3 contract. Do not start architecture comparisons before this passes. - [ ] **1 · Serving topology.** Compare EP8 on 8 GPUs with EP16 on 16. Report per-GPU throughput and zero-preemption capacity. Test EP32 on 32 only if EP16 remains efficient and more capacity is needed. - [ ] **2 · Global KV heads.** Compare local/global `12/6` with `12/12` and `12/2`. These two alternatives bound full and compressed global KV; add no other head counts. - [x] **3 · Global-attention frequency.** Compare global attention every six layers with every four. [Result: #8017](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8017): keep global attention every six layers. - [x] **4 · Sliding window.** Compare 512, 1,024, and 2,048. [Result: #8017](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8017): 512 is cheapest; 1,024 has a small measured cost; 2,048 has no inference-cost case in these measurements. - [ ] **5 · SConv4.** Compare the full four-site `sconv4` path on versus off. Profile once only if the delta is material or health is abnormal. - [ ] **6 · Lightweight blocks.** Keep XSA, attention gate, and GatedNorm on in the anchor; briefly disable each one at a time. Treat this as one bundled gate, not three project tracks. For MoE geometry and EP topology, run both canonical dummy routing and the protocol's deterministic balanced-routing control. Run the primary matrix with R3 off; add R3-on controls for payload-changing candidates and finalists as specified in #7912.
P1 candidates requiring a modeling decision Modeling must mark each family **Include** or **Exclude with reason**. An included family needs one complete executable config. A missing serving path or failed measurement is not a quality rejection. - [ ] **7 · Width.** Compare the anchor with one complete `d7168` candidate. Treat `d8192` as a placement/performance-cliff probe unless modeling explicitly promotes it. Record every coupled shape change; do not label the whole bundle as width alone. - [ ] **8 · Expert pool size.** Compare `4/128/i3072` with exact `4/256/i3072`. Keep top-K and active expert width fixed. Run canonical and balanced routes; add no expert-count sweep. - [ ] **9 · Expert granularity.** Compare `4/128/i3072` with exact `8/256/i1536`, after modeling confirms matched total and active routed-MLP width. Run both route controls; add no granularity sweep. - [ ] **10 · Over-Encoding.** Compare the anchor with one modeling-confirmed mechanism and config. Measure one serving-cost pair; do not sweep mechanisms. - [ ] **11 · Wider attention.** Compare 48 query heads and local/global KV `12/6` with one bundled 64-query-head, `16/8` candidate. Treat query heads, attention width, and KV layout as one bundle. - [ ] **12 · Finalist.** If no P1 family is included, reuse the anchor evidence. If one is included, reuse its pair and add only missing finalist checks. If two or more are included, run one composed pair. Do not run a combinations matrix.
Non-blocking stretch candidates Run these only after required work, in this order, when modeling supplies one quality-viable config and capacity remains: - [ ] **13 · MLA.** Compare GQA with one exact MLA candidate. If modeling does not revive it, record `Deferred: no live quality candidate`. Do not sweep MLA or KV-matching variants. - [ ] **14 · Dense/MoE alternation.** After MLA closes, compare all-MoE with one matched dense/MoE candidate. Add no alternation-ratio sweep. - [ ] **15 · Smaller local KV.** Compare `12/6` with one exact smaller-local-KV shape at only 8K and 65K context. Add no head-count sweep. These boxes do not block the inference recommendation or hero-run readiness.
## Completion This tracker is complete when: - [ ] modeling has included or excluded every P1 family and supplied exact configs for included candidates; - [ ] benchmark health and every required architecture box have valid results; - [ ] every included P1 candidate has a valid result or a recorded, modeling-owned exclusion; - [ ] the reference, attention/KV finalists, every memory-cliff candidate, and the final model pass the four-turn 65K trajectory; - [ ] the reference and attention/KV finalists pass the one-turn 131K capacity stress; and - [ ] the final inference recommendation states the measured cost, confidence, and remaining caveat, and is shared with modeling before architecture freeze. Lower precision, remaining serving-only tuning, MTP speculative decoding, and a full synchronous RL-loop benchmark belong in follow-ups.
What each result packet must contain Create one subissue and result packet per experiment family, not per scalar value. Each main result contains: 1. the decision question and the one changed property or declared bundle; 2. a compact reference/candidate table with generated tok/s/GPU, paired delta, load/KV/routing/R3 health, and repeat status; 3. immutable code, config, image, workload, Iris job, placement, and artifact links; and 4. a plain inference recommendation, confidence, and remaining caveat. For attention/KV candidates, include predicted and active KV bytes and zero-preemption resident sequences per DP rank. For MoE candidates, include both routing fixtures and per-rank load. For width, include loaded weights, non-KV memory, available KV bytes, and any EP16 cliff. If a candidate changes the R3 payload shape, include its cost and use the protocol's R3-off diagnostic trigger. Keep negative results. A tuned diagnostic never replaces the fixed-setting result, and no candidate is rejected without a recorded human decision.
Why the gated and stretch candidates are bounded - [#7673](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7673) retains `d7168` as a planning candidate and treats `d8192` as an unmeasured width cliff; neither issue entry supplies a full executable config. - [#7201's top-4-of-256 proposal](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201#issuecomment-5054192424) doubles the resident expert pool while keeping top-K and active expert width fixed. This is distinct from the top-8-of-256 granularity candidate. - The [wider-attention probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201#issuecomment-5125065343) and [follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201#issuecomment-5125219118) propose the 64-head `16/8` bundle but do not establish target quality or RL inference performance. - [Over-Encoding](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7368#issuecomment-5021519909) has small-scale training evidence but no B200 serving result. - Existing [MLA results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7381#issuecomment-5018382492) favor GQA, so MLA runs only if modeling revives one candidate. - [Dense/MoE evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6885) is positive small-scale training evidence, not a target-scale model decision or B200 serving result.
References - [#7201: GB200 architecture TPS tracker](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201) - [#7673: provisional pretraining and RL timelines](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7673) - [#7706: serving topology study](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7706) - [#7374: MLA ablation tracker](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7374) - [#7585: SConv quality tests](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7585) - [#7164: train-to-serve routing parity](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7164) - [#7248: R3 payload and transport measurements](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7248)

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment tested NorMuonH as a matrix-parameter optimizer swap for Grug MoE, using NorMuon's output-axis normalization inside the existing hyperball update while keeping the same Adam routing for embeddings, routers, vector/scalar leaves, and the lm head as the AdamH baseline. Gate 1 completed at d512 and d768: NorMuonH beat the v16 AdamH baseline at both scales and was effectively tied with the corrected MuonH matrix-swap baseline, with about 1.34x wall-clock speedup at d512 and 1.28x at d768 versus AdamH. The recommendation from the recorded result is that NorMuonH passed the first gate and justified the already-launched gate-2 sweep, but its measured advantage over MuonH was only about 1%.

### Helpful links
- Final Gate 1 result comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5598#issuecomment-4425980304
- W&B report: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/NorMuonH-vs-MuonH-vs-v16-AdamH-—-gate-1--VmlldzoxNjg0Nzc3Nw==
- Implementation PR: #5597
- Paired MuonH comparison: #5596
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Evaluate a Grug MoE optimizer ablation that uses NorMuon inside the existing hyperball-style update for every matrix-shaped parameter except the lm head (`output_proj`), which remains on AdamH. Vector and scalar leaves remain on Adam.

The key implementation detail is axis convention. NorMuon is written in the paper for matrices `W in R^{m x n}` and tracks one second-moment statistic per row using `mean_cols(O * O)`. Grug stores dense matrices as `(fan_in, fan_out)`, so this experiment maps NorMuon's neuron/output statistic to the trailing output axis. For stacked MoE tensors `(num_experts, fan_in, fan_out)`, the statistic has shape `(num_experts, fan_out)`.

Exact initiating prompts:

> Additionally test using NorMuon instead of Muon inside hyperball (please be careful about dimension as jax has slightly different convention) https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05491v1

> Create a separate issue for it to track experiment status and continue to follow moe.md

## Hypothesis or Goal

NorMuon's output-axis adaptive normalization after orthogonalization may improve over the MuonH matrix swap by reducing imbalance across output/neuron update magnitudes while preserving the low-condition-number Muon direction and Grug hyperball norm preservation.

Gate 1 tests d512 at 2.19e17 FLOPs and d768 at 1.70e18 FLOPs against the README baseline table, plus the paired MuonH matrix-swap issue #5596.

### Links

* Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05491v1
* Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/moe-normuonh-matrix-sweep.md`
* Launcher: `experiments/grug/moe/normuonh_matrix_sweep.py`
* Paired MuonH issue: #5596
* Implementation PR: #5597

## Results

Not launched yet. Initial local validation passed focused optimizer tests, including a state-shape check that pins Grug's output-axis NorMuon convention.

Pi sessions converted to ATIF by #10972 omit three fields available during a trial: assistant reasoning, tool error status, and final token and step counts. The missing data limits episode inspection and can make failed tool calls appear successful.

Done when:
- Pi reasoning content is retained in the ATIF trajectory without changing the visible assistant answer.
- Tool result error flags are represented in the corresponding ATIF observations.
- Final token and step counts collected during the scenario appear in ATIF final metrics, with a test comparing them to the source session.

See the approval review on #10972 for the three gaps.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Pi `message_end` assistant blocks contain `thinking`, but `_assistant_step` only extracts text and tool calls; `_attach_tool_result` drops `isError`. `final_metrics` recomputes prompt and completion counts separately from `AgentContext`, omits cached tokens and cost, and has no source-session parity test.

**Relevant code**
- [`pi.py#L752-L793`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L752-L793) — collected scenario totals
- [`pi.py#L863-L925`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L863-L925) — ATIF final metrics
- [`pi.py#L966-L1060`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L966-L1060) — assistant and observation conversion

# Proposed Fix

`pi.txt` → `populate_context_post_run` → `_trajectory_from_events` loses thinking and error status at the step builders, then independently sums final usage. Map thinking blocks to `Step.reasoning_content`, carry `isError` in `ObservationResult.extra`, and fill ATIF final metrics from the collected context totals while keeping `total_steps` tied to emitted steps. Compare the resulting metrics and fields against the source session in the Pi conversion test.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
One pod whose container exec fails in the runtime makes every Iris controller control tick raise. While that pod stays in that state, the controller dispatches and cleans up nothing.

On cw-rno2a, no task attempt has reached RUNNING in the controller database since 2026-11-06 21:59 UTC. 80 tasks across 8 users sit in `TASK_STATE_ASSIGNED`. Their pods can exist and run, because `sync` applies new pods before the polling step that raises. The controller never records them as running, so jobs that wait on a child's terminal state stall. The `marin` and `cw-us-east-02a` clusters are unaffected. The controller (build `260d937671`) logs this on every tick:

```
iris.cluster.controller.controller Control tick failed
  controller.py:1087 _control_tick -> self.backend.reconcile(...)
  backends/k8s/tasks.py:2658 sync -> self._poll_pods(...)
  backends/k8s/tasks.py:3278 _poll_pods -> self._finalize_task_outputs(entry, pod_name, pod)
  backends/k8s/tasks.py:3173 _finalize_task_outputs -> self.kubectl.exec(pod_name, ["touch", OUTPUT_RELEASE_PATH], ...)
  platforms/k8s/service.py:760 exec -> ExecResult(returncode=resp.returncode, ...)
  kubernetes/stream/ws_client.py:292 returncode -> int(err['details']['causes'][0]['message'])
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'Internal error occurred: error executing command in container: failed to exec in container: failed to start exec "f3d16a5d…": OCI runtime exec f…'
```

When the runtime cannot start the exec, kubernetes-client 36.0.3 parses a non-numeric failure cause as the exit code. `CloudK8sService.exec` catches only `ApiException` and `TransportError`, and `_finalize_task_outputs` catches only `KubectlError`. The `ValueError` therefore escapes `sync`, `reconcile` and `_control_tick`, and the tick never commits. The same code is on current `main`.

Reproduce (unit level): call `CloudK8sService.exec` with a closed exec stream whose `returncode` is `kubernetes.stream.ws_client.WSClient.returncode`, and whose error channel returns `{"status": "Failure", "details": {"causes": [{"message": "Internal error occurred: ... OCI runtime exec failed"}]}}`. It raises `ValueError` instead of returning a failed `ExecResult`. Live: submit any job to cw-rno2a, for example `iris --cluster=cw-rno2a job run --cpu 0.1 --memory 256MB -- echo ok`. It stays ASSIGNED in the controller database. `iris rpc controller get-kubernetes-cluster-status` is not reliable here: its pod cache refreshes inside the failing tick, so it is stale.

No test covers this. `test_cloud_k8s_service.py` fakes exec streams only with integer return codes, and no provider or controller test asserts that one pod's unexpected error leaves the rest of `sync` and the tick intact.

Expected: an exec that cannot start returns a failed `ExecResult` (or a `KubectlError`), and one pod's failure in `_poll_pods` cannot abort reconcile for the whole cluster. Tests cover both.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 ## Research

`CloudK8sService.exec` reads the Kubernetes websocket's `returncode`, whose client parser raises `ValueError` when the runtime reports an OCI exec failure as a nonnumeric cause. `_finalize_task_outputs` catches only `KubectlError`, so that exception escapes pod polling and aborts the controller tick.

Relevant code:
- [`service.py#L760`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33748734802cbb9839a99731260bcc1977e1530e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/service.py#L760): reads the websocket exit code.
- [`tasks.py#L3179`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33748734802cbb9839a99731260bcc1977e1530e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L3179): releases the output uploader.
- [`tasks.py#L3285`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33748734802cbb9839a99731260bcc1977e1530e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L3285): calls finalization during pod polling.

## Proposed Fix

Return a failed `ExecResult` when the websocket exit code is malformed. Keep output release failures local to that pod so polling can process other tasks, and add regressions for both boundaries.

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This eval experiment tried to reproduce Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores on Marin for four large MoE baselines using Terminus 2, three attempts per task, a 250-turn limit, a 7,200-second agent timeout, and the pinned TB2.1 dataset. The main result is mixed. Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4 reproduced the AAII point estimate almost exactly at 54.09% versus 53.93%. Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 was still preliminary in the posted table, at 42.34% versus 47.57% with 110/111 completed trials and 156 trials remaining. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 cleared the infrastructure-success gate but missed parity badly, scoring 56.23% versus AAII's 78.65% with no confirmed protocol discrepancy. GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4 produced no valid cohort because the checkpoint could not be served with the required context under the tested single-node geometry. The follow-up work is to finish Qwen, isolate the DeepSeek score gap, and rerun GLM with a serving geometry that preserves the intended context budget.

### Helpful links
- Experiment summary comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8261#issuecomment-5299403446
- Versioned launch configs and artifacts: https://huggingface.co/datasets/penfever/large-model-agentic-eval-parity-tb21-aa/tree/main/artifacts
- Baseline/context comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8261#issuecomment-5299504940
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Human Authored tl;dr

WHAT THIS IS: The purpose of this experiment was to try to reproduce AAII tb2.1 eval scores on the Marin cluster on some strong baselines.
WHY WE DID IT: Exercise Marin's eval pipeline and thoroughly understand how AAII executes tb2.1, since minor differences in protocol can dramatically impact scores.
RESULT: Picked four models; Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4, GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4. GLM 5.2 did not run (needs either pipeline parallel or B200s or possibly both). Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4 succeeded. Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 is slightly below parity but pretty close. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 is way below parity and there's no obvious discrepancy so I'm not sure why.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 ## Experiment summary

This experiment compares Marin's Terminal-Bench 2.1 results with the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (AAII) for four large MoE models. The protocol uses Terminus 2, three attempts per task (267 trials), a 250-turn limit, a 7,200-second agent timeout, and the pinned `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@sha256:7d7bdc1cbedad549fc1140404bd4dc45e5fd0ea7c4186773687d177ad3a0699a` dataset. Marin used Daytona sandboxes; AAII used E2B.

| Model | AAII | Marin | Delta | Scoreable trials | Infrastructure success | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4 | 53.93% | 54.09% | +0.16 pp | 257/267 | 96.25% | Reproduced |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | 47.57% | 42.34% | -5.23 pp | 110/111 completed | 99.10% | Preliminary; 156 trials remain |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | 78.65% | 56.23% | -22.42 pp | 265/267 | 99.25% | Valid Marin result; parity failed |
| GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4 | 77.90% | — | — | 0/267 | 0.00% | No valid cohort |

The Qwen rerun aligns the 262,144-token serving context and 81,920-token generation limit across vLLM and Terminus 2. Its current 42.34% mean comprises 48 successes and 62 zeros. Thirteen `AgentTimeoutError` trials received verifier scores and are valid; one `VerifierTimeoutError` is an infrastructure failure.

Nemotron reproduces the AAII point estimate within 0.16 percentage points. DeepSeek clears the 90% infrastructure gate but remains 22.42 points below AAII with no confirmed protocol discrepancy. GLM did not produce a valid result because the AWQ checkpoint could not be served with the required context under the tested single-node geometry; pipeline parallelism or B200 capacity remains to be tested.

Checkpoint and environment differences limit the comparison. AAII evaluated unquantized Qwen and GLM checkpoints and BF16 Nemotron, while Marin used Qwen FP8, GLM AWQ INT4, and Nemotron NVFP4. DeepSeek used the same checkpoint family. The sandbox provider also differs.

Next steps are to finish the Qwen cohort, isolate the DeepSeek score gap, and rerun GLM with a serving geometry that preserves the intended context budget.

🤖 Official and independent baselines put these results in context:

| Model | Vendor SWE-Bench Verified | Vendor Terminal-Bench | Artificial Analysis TB 2.1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B | 72.0 | 49.4 (TB 2.0) | 47.57 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | not reported | 82.7 (TB 2.1) | 78.65 |
| Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B | 69.5 | 53.9 (TB 2.1) | 53.93 |
| GLM-5.2 | not reported | 81.0 (TB 2.1) | 77.90 |

Artificial Analysis v4.1.1 runs 89 tasks three times with Terminus-2 in E2B and reports pass@1. Only DeepSeek is an exact checkpoint match: its entry uses `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`; the other entries differ in precision or checkpoint from this campaign. Vendor conditions also vary. GLM reports 256K context and 48K maximum output with a four-hour timeout; NVIDIA documents thinking-mode sampling and an eight-repeat Terminal-Bench recipe, but its public recipe names TB 2.0 while the card reports TB 2.1; Qwen does not publish a complete resource-limit recipe. These figures are therefore comparison targets, not zero-confound parity baselines.

The official Terminal-Bench leaderboard did not contain any of the four exact campaign targets when checked on August 11, 2026. Current DeepSeek and GLM-5.2 model materials also do not report SWE-Bench Verified; older family results are not transferable to these checkpoints.
